claim: The dopamine D2 receptor has two splice variants, D2S (Short) and D2L (Long).
source: The dopamine D2 receptor has two splice variants, D2S (Short) and D2L (Long).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without requiring experimental support in this manuscript.

claim: In dopamine neurons, both D2S and D2L variants can act as autoreceptors to regulate neuronal excitability and dopamine release.
source: In dopamine neurons, both variants can act as autoreceptors to regulate neuronal excitability and dopamine release, but the roles of each variant are incompletely characterized.
evidence: This statement draws on established scientific knowledge about D2 receptor function.

claim: A previous study used viral receptor expression in D2 receptor knockout mice to show distinct effects of calcium signaling on D2S and D2L autoreceptor function.
source: In a previous study we used viral receptor expression in D2 receptor knockout mice to show distinct effects of calcium signaling on D2S and D2L autoreceptor function (Gantz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Gantz et al., 2015.

claim: Cocaine-induced plasticity of D2 receptor desensitization observed in wild type mice was not recapitulated with viral receptor expression.
source: However, the cocaine-induced plasticity of D2 receptor desensitization observed in wild type mice was not recapitulated with this method of receptor expression.
evidence: This is a statement about prior experimental findings that contrasts with wild type observations.

claim: Following a single in vivo cocaine exposure, the desensitization of D2 receptors from neurons expressing only the D2S variant was reduced.
source: Following a single in vivo cocaine exposure, the desensitization of D2 receptors from neurons expressing only the D2S variant was reduced.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: Cocaine exposure did not reduce desensitization in D2L-expressing neurons.
source: This did not occur in D2L-expressing neurons, indicating differential drug-induced plasticity between the variants.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 1C.

claim: Dopamine D2 autoreceptors decrease neuronal excitability when activated by dendrodendritic release of dopamine in the midbrain.
source: Dopamine D2 autoreceptors decrease neuronal excitability when activated by dendrodendritic release of dopamine in the midbrain.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about D2 autoreceptor function.

claim: The D2S and D2L variants differ by a 29 amino acid section in the third intracellular loop.
source: The D2 receptor has short (D2S) and long (D2L) splice variants that differ by a 29 amino acid section in the third intracellular loop.
evidence: This is stated as established structural knowledge about the D2 receptor variants.

claim: Both D2S and D2L variants are expressed in dopamine neurons and function effectively as autoreceptors.
source: While both variants are expressed in dopamine neurons and function effectively as autoreceptors (Khan et al., 1998; Jang et al., 2011; Dragicevic et al., 2014; Jomphe et al., 2006; Neve et al., 2013), subtle differences have been reported suggesting the variants are not redundant.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The D2S receptor desensitizes and internalizes to a greater degree than D2L.
source: The D2S receptor desensitizes and internalizes to a greater degree than D2L (Liu et al., 1992; Itokawa et al., 1996; Ito et al., 1999; Morris et al., 2007; Thibault et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Desensitization of the D2S receptor-dependent activation of GIRK conductance was greater than D2L and was dependent on the level of intracellular calcium buffering.
source: Desensitization of the D2S receptor-dependent activation of G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK) conductance was also greater and was dependent on the level of intracellular calcium buffering (Gantz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gantz et al., 2015.

claim: Desensitization of the D2 receptor is decreased following in vivo acute drug exposure to ethanol.
source: Desensitization of the D2 receptor is decreased following in vivo acute drug exposure to ethanol (Perra et al., 2011), cocaine (Dragicevic et al., 2014; Gantz et al., 2015), or L-DOPA (Dragicevic et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Perra et al., 2011.

claim: Desensitization of the D2 receptor is decreased following in vivo acute drug exposure to cocaine.
source: Desensitization of the D2 receptor is decreased following in vivo acute drug exposure to ethanol (Perra et al., 2011), cocaine (Dragicevic et al., 2014; Gantz et al., 2015), or L-DOPA (Dragicevic et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dragicevic et al., 2014 and Gantz et al., 2015.

claim: Desensitization of the D2 receptor is decreased following in vivo acute drug exposure to L-DOPA.
source: Desensitization of the D2 receptor is decreased following in vivo acute drug exposure to ethanol (Perra et al., 2011), cocaine (Dragicevic et al., 2014; Gantz et al., 2015), or L-DOPA (Dragicevic et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dragicevic et al., 2014.

claim: A reduction in desensitization following drug exposure would conceivably result in a more effective autoreceptor and therefore reduced neuronal excitability during the next high dopamine situation.
source: A reduction in desensitization following drug exposure would conceivably result in a more effective autoreceptor (and therefore reduced neuronal excitability) during the next high dopamine situation, which would have widespread effects on dopamine signaling throughout the brain.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the functional consequences of reduced desensitization.

claim: Studies using viral expression of single D2 receptor variants in D2-KO mice were inconclusive in determining whether the plasticity induced by cocaine resulted from adaptation of a single variant or an altered ratio of splice variant expression/function.
source: However, studies using viral expression of single D2 receptor variants in D2-KO mice were inconclusive in determining whether the plasticity induced by cocaine resulted from adaptation of a single variant, or perhaps an altered ratio of splice variant expression/function (Gantz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim references prior work by Gantz et al., 2015 and its limitations.

claim: A single treatment of animals with cocaine reduced acute desensitization of the D2S variant.
source: The results show that a single treatment of animals with cocaine reduced acute desensitization of the D2S variant.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data in Figure 1B.

claim: Treatment with cocaine did not alter the expression of either D2 receptor variant.
source: Treatment with cocaine did not alter the expression of either D2 receptor variant, and the desensitization of the D2L variant was not changed.
evidence: This is supported by current density measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: The desensitization of the D2L variant was not changed by cocaine treatment.
source: Treatment with cocaine did not alter the expression of either D2 receptor variant, and the desensitization of the D2L variant was not changed.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 1C.

claim: Plasticity in D2 receptor signaling induced by a single cocaine treatment results from adaptation of the D2S variant.
source: Thus, it appears that plasticity in D2 receptor signaling induced by a single cocaine treatment results from adaptation of the D2S variant.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: In wild type mice, D2-GIRK currents desensitized to a greater extent with weak calcium buffering EGTA internal solution compared to strong buffering BAPTA internal.
source: D2-GIRK currents from wild type mice desensitized to a greater extent with the weak calcium buffering EGTA internal solution compared to the strong buffering BAPTA internal.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: With the use of EGTA internal solution, the D2-GIRK current desensitized significantly less in cells from animals that were treated with cocaine in wild type mice.
source: With the use of EGTA (and not BAPTA) internal solution the D2-GIRK current desensitized significantly less in cells from animals that were treated with cocaine (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The results from experiments with the D2L-KO mice (expressing D2S only) were similar to experiments in wild type mice.
source: The results from experiments with the D2L-KO mice (expressing D2S only) were similar to experiments in wild type mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of experimental data from Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, the decline in the quinpirole current with EGTA internal was greater than with BAPTA internal.
source: The decline in the quinpirole current with EGTA internal was greater than with BAPTA internal and was significantly reduced following in vivo cocaine treatment (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, the decline in the quinpirole current was significantly reduced following in vivo cocaine treatment.
source: The decline in the quinpirole current with EGTA internal was greater than with BAPTA internal and was significantly reduced following in vivo cocaine treatment (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In D2S-KO mice (expressing only D2L), some calcium sensitivity in current decline was still present.
source: In D2S-KO mice (expressing only D2L), some calcium sensitivity in current decline was still present (EGTA currents declined significantly more than BAPTA currents), but treatment with cocaine had no effect in these animals (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Treatment with cocaine had no effect on current decline in D2S-KO mice.
source: In D2S-KO mice (expressing only D2L), some calcium sensitivity in current decline was still present (EGTA currents declined significantly more than BAPTA currents), but treatment with cocaine had no effect in these animals (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: In wild type animals there were significant overall effects of internal solution on the decline of I-quinpirole.
source: In wild type animals there were significant overall effects of internal solution (F(1, 30)=23.57, p<0.001) and cocaine treatment (20 mg/kg, F(1, 30)=4.259, p=0.048) on the decline of I-quinpirole.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In wild type animals there were significant overall effects of cocaine treatment on the decline of I-quinpirole.
source: In wild type animals there were significant overall effects of internal solution (F(1, 30)=23.57, p<0.001) and cocaine treatment (20 mg/kg, F(1, 30)=4.259, p=0.048) on the decline of I-quinpirole.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In wild type animals, the decline using BAPTA internal was less than that using EGTA in both naïve and cocaine-treated conditions.
source: Post-hoc analyses indicate that in both treatment conditions the decline using BAPTA (B) internal was less than that using EGTA (E, p<0.001 for naïve and coc-treated).
evidence: This is supported by post-hoc statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In wild type animals with EGTA internal, there was significantly reduced decline following cocaine treatment.
source: Additionally, with EGTA internal there was significantly reduced decline following cocaine treatment (p=0.049, n = 7–9 neurons from 5 to 8 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, there was an overall effect of internal solution on current decline.
source: In mice in which the long isoform of the D2 receptor has been knocked out (D2L-KO), there was an overall effect of internal solution (F(1, 32)=37.09, p<0.001), but not of cocaine treatment (F (1, 32)=2.917, p=0.097).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, there was no overall effect of cocaine treatment on current decline.
source: In mice in which the long isoform of the D2 receptor has been knocked out (D2L-KO), there was an overall effect of internal solution (F(1, 32)=37.09, p<0.001), but not of cocaine treatment (F (1, 32)=2.917, p=0.097).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, there was significantly more decline when using EGTA internal than BAPTA internal in both naïve and cocaine-treated conditions.
source: In post hoc analyses, there was significantly more decline when using EGTA internal than BAPTA internal in both treatment conditions (p<0.001 for naïve, p=0.002 for cocaine-treated), and the decline was significantly reduced following drug exposure when EGTA internal was used (p=0.021, n = 8–12 neurons from 4 to 7 mice).
evidence: This is supported by post-hoc statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, the decline was significantly reduced following drug exposure when EGTA internal was used.
source: In post hoc analyses, there was significantly more decline when using EGTA internal than BAPTA internal in both treatment conditions (p<0.001 for naïve, p=0.002 for cocaine-treated), and the decline was significantly reduced following drug exposure when EGTA internal was used (p=0.021, n = 8–12 neurons from 4 to 7 mice).
evidence: This is supported by post-hoc statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In D2S-KO mice, there was an overall effect of internal solution on current decline.
source: In animals with the short isoform of the D2 receptor knocked out (D2S-KO), there was an overall effect of internal solution (F(1, 28)=21.24, p<0.001) with EGTA currents declining significantly more that those of BAPTA in both treatment conditions (p=0.001 for naïve, p=0.007 for coc-treated, n = 7–9 neurons from 4 to 7 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: In D2S-KO mice, EGTA currents declined significantly more than those of BAPTA in both naïve and cocaine-treated conditions.
source: In animals with the short isoform of the D2 receptor knocked out (D2S-KO), there was an overall effect of internal solution (F(1, 28)=21.24, p<0.001) with EGTA currents declining significantly more that those of BAPTA in both treatment conditions (p=0.001 for naïve, p=0.007 for coc-treated, n = 7–9 neurons from 4 to 7 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cocaine treatment caused no change in desensitization of the D2-GIRK current in D2S-KO mice.
source: Cocaine treatment caused no change in desensitization of the D2-GIRK current in this genotype.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: L-type calcium channels are a source of calcium that impacts D2 receptor signaling.
source: The L-type calcium channels (Dragicevic et al., 2014; Gantz et al., 2015) and intracellular calcium stores (Perra et al., 2011; Gantz et al., 2015) are two sources of calcium that impact D2 receptor signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Intracellular calcium stores are a source of calcium that impacts D2 receptor signaling.
source: The L-type calcium channels (Dragicevic et al., 2014; Gantz et al., 2015) and intracellular calcium stores (Perra et al., 2011; Gantz et al., 2015) are two sources of calcium that impact D2 receptor signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: There are likely calcium binding proteins that act as intermediaries between calcium and the D2 receptor.
source: However, there are likely calcium binding proteins that act as intermediaries between the ion and the D2 receptor.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from known biology.

claim: The intracellular domains of the D2 receptor can bind calmodulin.
source: Indeed, the intracellular domains of the D2 receptor can bind calmodulin (Bofill-Cardona et al., 2000; Liu et al., 2007), NCS-1 (Kabbani et al., 2002; Dragicevic et al., 2014; Pandalaneni et al., 2015), and S100B (Liu et al., 2008; Dempsey and Shaw, 2011) among other potential calcium sensitive proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The intracellular domains of the D2 receptor can bind NCS-1.
source: Indeed, the intracellular domains of the D2 receptor can bind calmodulin (Bofill-Cardona et al., 2000; Liu et al., 2007), NCS-1 (Kabbani et al., 2002; Dragicevic et al., 2014; Pandalaneni et al., 2015), and S100B (Liu et al., 2008; Dempsey and Shaw, 2011) among other potential calcium sensitive proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The intracellular domains of the D2 receptor can bind S100B.
source: Indeed, the intracellular domains of the D2 receptor can bind calmodulin (Bofill-Cardona et al., 2000; Liu et al., 2007), NCS-1 (Kabbani et al., 2002; Dragicevic et al., 2014; Pandalaneni et al., 2015), and S100B (Liu et al., 2008; Dempsey and Shaw, 2011) among other potential calcium sensitive proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The D2S is more calcium sensitive than D2L.
source: The present results show that while the D2S is more calcium sensitive than D2L, the long variant maintains some calcium sensitivity as evidenced by decreased desensitization when calcium is strongly buffered by the BAPTA internal solution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The D2L variant maintains some calcium sensitivity as evidenced by decreased desensitization when calcium is strongly buffered by the BAPTA internal solution.
source: The present results show that while the D2S is more calcium sensitive than D2L, the long variant maintains some calcium sensitivity as evidenced by decreased desensitization when calcium is strongly buffered by the BAPTA internal solution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: The calcium sensitivity of the D2 receptor involves multiple sources.
source: One explanation is that the calcium sensitivity of the D2 receptor involves multiple sources.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed data.

claim: Recent imaging of endogenous D2 receptors revealed a clustered and static localization.
source: Recent imaging of endogenous D2 receptors revealed a clustered and static localization (Robinson et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Robinson et al., 2017.

claim: It is possible that an array of proteins, potentially including several that are calcium sensitive, forms a complex with D2 receptors modulating their placement and signaling.
source: It is possible that an array of proteins, potentially including several that are calcium sensitive, forms a complex with D2 receptors modulating their placement and signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on inference from the data and prior knowledge.

claim: Two intronic single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the DRD2 gene cause an increase in D2L expression relative to D2S.
source: Adaptation in one D2 receptor variant but not the other is relevant to studies in humans that have identified two intronic single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the DRD2 gene that cause an increase in D2L expression relative to D2S.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from human genetic studies.

claim: SNPs in the DRD2 gene that increase D2L expression have been found to be associated with cocaine abuse.
source: These SNPs have been found to be associated with cocaine (Moyer et al., 2011; Levran et al., 2015), alcohol (Sasabe et al., 2007), and opioid abuse (Clarke et al., 2014; Levran et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SNPs in the DRD2 gene that increase D2L expression have been found to be associated with alcohol abuse.
source: These SNPs have been found to be associated with cocaine (Moyer et al., 2011; Levran et al., 2015), alcohol (Sasabe et al., 2007), and opioid abuse (Clarke et al., 2014; Levran et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sasabe et al., 2007.

claim: SNPs in the DRD2 gene that increase D2L expression have been found to be associated with opioid abuse.
source: These SNPs have been found to be associated with cocaine (Moyer et al., 2011; Levran et al., 2015), alcohol (Sasabe et al., 2007), and opioid abuse (Clarke et al., 2014; Levran et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The ratio of D2 autoreceptor variants could be important in drug related behaviors.
source: However, because dopamine neurons can express either variant, the ratio of D2 autoreceptor variants could very well be important in drug related behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental findings and prior knowledge.

claim: Increased presence of the D2L variant as the autoreceptor would alter the dopamine reward circuitry because this variant desensitizes less.
source: Increased presence of the D2L variant as the autoreceptor would alter the dopamine reward circuitry because this variant desensitizes less (suggesting it is a more efficacious autoreceptor) and does not appear to adapt following a single cocaine exposure.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: The D2L variant does not appear to adapt following a single cocaine exposure.
source: Increased presence of the D2L variant as the autoreceptor would alter the dopamine reward circuitry because this variant desensitizes less (suggesting it is a more efficacious autoreceptor) and does not appear to adapt following a single cocaine exposure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: Following cocaine exposure, desensitization of the D2S variant adapts to resemble the D2L variant.
source: Furthermore, following cocaine exposure desensitization of the D2S variant adapts to resemble the D2L variant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing D2S and D2L desensitization patterns.

claim: In this assay, preexisting prevalence of the D2L variant would resemble a previous cocaine experience.
source: In this assay, preexisting prevalence of the D2L variant would resemble a previous cocaine experience.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: A previous study using viral D2 receptor variant expression found no calcium-dependent desensitization of D2L and no cocaine-induced adaptation of either variant.
source: The present results are in some respects at odds with the previous study that used viral D2 receptor variant expression and found no calcium-dependent desensitization of D2L and no cocaine-induced adaptation of either variant (Gantz et al., 2015), rather than decreased calcium-dependent desensitization of D2L and selective cocaine-induced adaptation of D2S.
evidence: This claim references findings from Gantz et al., 2015.

claim: Virally transduced D2 receptors may have altered expression levels (often superphysiological) resulting in reduced sensitivity to adaptive mechanisms.
source: A possible explanation is that virally transduced D2 receptors have altered expression levels (often superphysiological) resulting in reduced sensitivity to adaptive mechanisms.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy between viral expression and knockout mouse results.

claim: In wild type mice, there was an overall significant effect of internal solution on D2-GIRK current density.
source: In wild type mice, there was an overall significant effect of internal solution on D2-GIRK current density (pA/pF, F(1, 30)=76.32, p<0.001).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In wild type mice, the current density was greater when using the strong calcium buffering BAPTA internal solution compared with the weak buffering EGTA internal solution.
source: The current density was greater when using the strong calcium buffering BAPTA (B) internal solution compared with the weak buffering EGTA (E) internal solution (p<0.001 for naïve and coc-treated, n = 7–11 neurons from 5 to 7 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In wild type mice, there was no difference in D2-GIRK current density between naïve and cocaine-treated groups.
source: There was no difference between naïve and cocaine-treated groups.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, there was an overall significant effect of internal solution on D2-GIRK current density.
source: From D2L-KO mice, there was an overall significant effect of internal solution (F(1, 32)=12.85, p=0.001).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, the current density of the BAPTA group was significantly larger than that of EGTA in both naïve and cocaine-treated conditions.
source: The current density of the BAPTA group was significantly larger than that of EGTA in both naïve and coc-treated conditions (p=0.016 for naïve, p=0.016 for coc-treated, n = 7–12 neurons from 4 to 7 mice), however there was no difference between treatment conditions.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In D2L-KO mice, there was no difference in D2-GIRK current density between naïve and cocaine-treated conditions.
source: The current density of the BAPTA group was significantly larger than that of EGTA in both naïve and coc-treated conditions (p=0.016 for naïve, p=0.016 for coc-treated, n = 7–12 neurons from 4 to 7 mice), however there was no difference between treatment conditions.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In D2S-KO mice, there was no significant effect of internal solution or drug treatment on D2-GIRK current density.
source: In D2S-KO mice, there was no significant effect of internal solution or drug treatment (n = 7–9 neurons from 5 to 7 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A comparison between D2L-KO and D2S-KO groups reveals an overall significant effect of genotype on current density.
source: Additionally, a comparison between D2L-KO and D2S-KO groups reveals an overall significant effect of genotype on current density (F(1, 28)=5.27, p=0.029, two-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis comparing data from Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: The effect of genotype on current density is likely not due to differences in GIRK channel expression because GABAB-GIRK current density was not different between the D2L-KO and D2S-KO groups.
source: This effect is likely not due to differences in GIRK channel expression because GABAB-GIRK current density was not different between the groups (in pA/pF D2L-KO EGTA 16.3 ± 2.3, BAPTA 18.2 ± 3.6 vs. D2S-KO EGTA 16.0 ± 0.6, BAPTA 18.8 ± 1.2, p>0.05 two-way ANOVA, data not shown).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data comparing GABAB-GIRK currents between genotypes.

claim: It was speculated that D2L function is in some way occluded under basal conditions.
source: Because of the similarity of D2S-mediated responses to responses of neurons from wild type mice, despite the presence of mRNA for both subtypes (Khan et al., 1998; Jang et al., 2011; Dragicevic et al., 2014) and the ability of both to activate GIRKs (Jomphe et al., 2006; Neve et al., 2013; Gantz et al., 2015), it was speculated that D2L function is in some way occluded under basal conditions (Gantz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis cited from Gantz et al., 2015.

claim: The lower current density for D2L in this study, despite similar levels of expression of the splice variants in these two lines of mice, is consistent with the notion that D2L function is occluded.
source: The lower current density for D2L in this study, despite similar levels of expression of the splice variants in these two lines of mice (D. Radl, M. Chiacchiaretta, R. Lewis, K. Brami-Cherrier, L. Arcuri, & E. Borrelli, manuscript in preparation), is consistent with this notion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and unpublished observations.

claim: The lower current density for D2L and lack of calcium-dependent desensitization could both be explained if the D2L receptor were constitutively desensitized.
source: Alternatively, the lower current density for D2L and lack of calcium-dependent desensitization could both be explained if the D2L receptor were constitutively desensitized.
evidence: This is a speculative alternative explanation for the observed data.

claim: The desensitization of GABAB receptor-induced GIRK currents with baclofen was not sensitive to the two different internal solutions.
source: Importantly, the desensitization of GABAB receptor-induced GIRK currents with baclofen (30 µM) was not sensitive to the two different internal solutions and did not change in any genotype following cocaine exposure (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The desensitization of GABAB receptor-induced GIRK currents did not change in any genotype following cocaine exposure.
source: Importantly, the desensitization of GABAB receptor-induced GIRK currents with baclofen (30 µM) was not sensitive to the two different internal solutions and did not change in any genotype following cocaine exposure (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The calcium sensitive desensitization and the cocaine-induced adaptations are specific to the D2 receptor and not general to Gi-coupled GPCRs or GIRK channels.
source: Thus, the calcium sensitive desensitization and the cocaine-induced adaptations are specific to the D2 receptor and not general to Gi-coupled GPCRs or GIRK channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the GABAB receptor control experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: There were no significant effects of EGTA versus BAPTA internal solution on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents from wild type mice.
source: There were no significant effects of EGTA (E, 0.01 mM) versus BAPTA (B, 10 mM) internal solution or treatment condition (naïve versus coc-treated) on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents (I-baclofen) from (A) wild type mice, (B) D2L-KO mice, or (C) D2S-KO mice (p<0.05, n = 5–9 neurons from 3 to 6 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There were no significant effects of treatment condition on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents from wild type mice.
source: There were no significant effects of EGTA (E, 0.01 mM) versus BAPTA (B, 10 mM) internal solution or treatment condition (naïve versus coc-treated) on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents (I-baclofen) from (A) wild type mice, (B) D2L-KO mice, or (C) D2S-KO mice (p<0.05, n = 5–9 neurons from 3 to 6 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There were no significant effects of EGTA versus BAPTA internal solution on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents from D2L-KO mice.
source: There were no significant effects of EGTA (E, 0.01 mM) versus BAPTA (B, 10 mM) internal solution or treatment condition (naïve versus coc-treated) on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents (I-baclofen) from (A) wild type mice, (B) D2L-KO mice, or (C) D2S-KO mice (p<0.05, n = 5–9 neurons from 3 to 6 mice).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There were no significant effects of treatment condition on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents from D2L-KO mice.
source: There were no significant effects of EGTA (E, 0.01 mM) versus BAPTA (B, 10 mM) internal solution or treatment condition (naïve versus coc-treated) on the decline in GABAB-GIRK currents (I-baclofen) from (A) wild type mice, (B) D2L-KO mice, or (C) D2S-KO mice (p<0.05, n = 5–9 neurons from 3 to 6 mice).
